blindSummary:
This state/province was the epicentre and last holdout of the country's "LGBT-ideology-free" resolution wave. It was one of five regional authorities to adopt an anti-LGBT declaration (repealed 20 September 2021 only after a supranational body threatened to freeze its regional development funds), and one of its counties held the country's final surviving anti-LGBT family charter until an extraordinary-session repeal on 24 April 2025 — six years after the phenomenon began. The regional capital's mayor outright banned the 2019 equality march on security grounds; a district court later overturned the ban and the march proceeded, but the executive intent to exclude a visible LGBTQ public presence is on the record.

The resolutions were never criminal statutes, and the repeal was extrinsic — funding leverage rather than a change in local attitudes — so the de facto social climate that produced them persists. For a visitor, the practical exposure is being visibly trans at a public event in a small town of this state/province where the local authority resisted all external pressure until 2025. An international traveller-safety assessment (July 2026) graded this state/province in its most severe category.

LGBTQ-news report (2021): this state/province's regional assembly withdrew its 'anti-LGBT ideology' declaration after a supranational body threatened to freeze regional development funds - evidence the repeal was externally driven rather than an attitudinal shift.

Regional news (national language, 2019): the district court in this state/province's capital overturned the city mayor's ban on the second equality march, ruling the march could proceed; the mayor said he would not appeal - the judicial reversal of an executive attempt to exclude a visible LGBTQ public event.

National legal-current-affairs daily (national language, 2019): the capital's mayor banned the equality parade citing police-safety consultations; regional opposition parties called the decision undemocratic - the executive intent to exclude, on the record.
